newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees need to cut energy sector emissions.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees need to cut energy sector emissions.

text.p: European Union energy ministers agreed on Tuesday they should step up action to curb emissions of greenhouse gas, which are responsible for climate change, but they stepped back from making any specific commitments.

Ministers said measures such as increasing the share of renewable energy sources in the EU fuel mix to 12 percent, cutting subsidies on fossil fuels and imposing higher taxes on the worst polluters and energy guzzlers could all make a substantial contribution to combatting climate change.

But they did not explicitly commit themselves to these or other anti-pollution measures, merely inviting the EU's executive Commission to come forward with a comprehensive action plan at a future date.

The ministers' strategy statement forms part of EU preparations for an international climate change summit in Kyoto, Japan, in December, where some 150 nations will aim to agree on legally-binding cuts in greenhouse gases.
The 1992 Rio de Janeiro Earth Summit committed industrialised countries to reducing carbon dioxide emissions to 1990 levels by the year 2000.
Most of these developed countries, including most of the 15-member EU bloc, will fail to meet their Rio targets.
The EU has acknowledged it will need to make a supreme effort to reach this goal and its new target of a 15 percent cut in emissions from 1990 levels by the year 2010.
